title: Round five — the layout you described, and how it moves

steps.path: The sessions arrow at the top of the window, then Resume
steps.headline: When you jump to another conversation, the whole sheet arrives — not just the card.
steps.changed: Both recordings step down the same three conversations. LEFT is the quieter option: only the header card rises and the conversation under it fades. RIGHT is the change: the card, the conversation and the action card rise together as one. Yes keeps the right-hand one; No leaves the quieter left-hand one.
steps.notice: The rise itself is not a new invention — it is the arrival you already chose on 2026-09-02 for this exact event, changing which conversation you are looking at. The chat view uses it too, so the two surfaces move alike.
steps.risk: One clip plays once. The move takes about a third of a second, so watch the moment right after each click.

steps.path: The card at the foot of the conversation
steps.headline: The stacked action card takes about a fifth of the sheet. Should it always be open?
steps.notice: Stacked and matching the other resume surfaces is what you asked for; this is only about whether it stays open while you are reading.

options.label: Always open
pros: Everything about relaunching is in front of you the whole time.
Resume is always one press, from anywhere in the conversation.
cons: It takes a fifth of the sheet away from the conversation you came here to read.

options.label: A Resume bar that opens it
pros: The conversation gets the room back until the moment you decide to go in.
Resume is still one press; the model and the switches are the second.
cons: Which model it will relaunch on is out of sight until you open it.
The sheet changes height under you when it opens.
options.cost: A collapsed state, and somewhere to remember it.
